observations.observation: Read all3889 characters. A cost/benefit assessment of three dam options cites distinct source bases for repair, rebuild and replacement, then narrows the narrative to a new system. Its main dependency chain is unusually explicit: hydrodynamics supplies velocity/depth to candidate-site evaluation; a segmented difference model supplies construction/operation details; correcting that model for energy loss, tributaries and rainfall precedes dam-type choice; discrete discharge gears then define emergency strategies. The separate transition sentence introduces this internal five-stage route. Safety/cost balancing and emergency search therefore consume upstream outputs rather than appearing as unrelated tools. Unlike q33, this abstract reports no optimized dam count/location list; it claims most extreme conditions can be handled and errors have little effect without numerical bounds here. Preserve that limited evidential strength and original wording (including awkward 'rule out the best strategies'), not an inferred global guarantee. Several discretionary word breaks and competition-form fields remain unverified extraction defects. Formula/diagram correctness and hydrological factual claims were not checked.
